title: API · Assets
description: List all tokenized assets, or fetch one by id.
content: Assets Replace $API_BASE_URL in examples with your configured API base URL (see API Overview ).

title: API · Assets › List assets
content: Returns an array of asset objects. Query parameters (all optional) Name Type Notes asset_type string Filter by class: real_estate , invoice , commodity active boolean Filter by active status fields string Sparse fieldset: comma-separated list such as id,name,active . offset integer Skip the first N matching assets. Default: 0 . limit integer Page size. Default: 50 ; maximum: 100 . Results are paginated to keep large collections bounded. Use offset and limit together to walk the list in chunks. curl "$API_BASE_URL/assets?asset_type=real_estate&active=true&offset=0&limit=50" Response schema (per asset): Field Type Notes id number Registry id token_contract string Asset-token contract issuer string Issuer account name string symbol string asset_type string real_estate \ invoice \ commodity description string valuation_cents string Valuation in USD cents ( i128 string). Divide by 100 to get USD dollars. valuation_usd number Valuation in USD dollars ( f64 convenience float, equal to valuation_cents / 100 ). decimals number Number of decimal places used by this asset token (e.g. 2 ). total_supply string Total supply in base units ( i128 string in the token's decimals base). Divide by 10 ** decimals to get the human-readable token amount. holders number Addresses with a positive balance active boolean paused boolean compliance_contract string Gate for this asset created_at_ledger number indexed_at_ledger number Most recent ledger successfully indexed for this asset index_error string or null Per-asset index error, if the latest refresh failed Example curl $API_BASE_URL/assets [ { "id": 1, "token_contract": "CBMCWLSQSWUTLUJFCNBHNBSXMUM3XU7NAQ5TSNERW4HA4ZZBYHLG4ECZ", "issuer": "GAIQGTOBTTLLDJ4SWGGESM7UWJ2DI4K3ZNHUSHPDKJL2IE5FKY3BSRAA", "name": "Manhattan Loft", "symbol": "MLOFT", "asset_type": "real_estate", "description": "A tokenized loft in Manhattan", "valuation_cents": "500000000", "valuation_usd": 5000000.0, "decimals": 2, "total_supply": "1000000", "holders": 1, "active": true, "paused": false, "compliance_contract": "CBUERYDM7DXTZLLKDBRJKUBPFJ7M4OSUN4T7XKUARU345RLXNAIQD2IU", "created_at_ledger": 3502885, "indexed_at_ledger": 3502885, "index_error": null } ]

title: API · Assets › Get an asset
content: Path parameters Name Type Notes id number Registry id (e.g. 1 ) Example curl $API_BASE_URL/assets/1 Returns a single asset object with the schema above. You can also request a sparse fieldset with ?fields= ; for example: curl "$API_BASE_URL/assets/1?fields=id,name,active,indexed_at_ledger" Errors { "error": "not_found", "message": "no asset with id 999" } Returned with status 404 when no asset has the given id. A non-numeric id ( /assets/abc ) is rejected with 400 by the router. Both total_supply and valuation_cents are 128-bit integers returned as strings to prevent rounding in JavaScript runtimes. // 1. Converting total_supply (base units to display tokens): // Given total_supply = "1000000" and decimals = 2: const rawSupply = BigInt(asset.total_supply); const displaySupply = Number(rawSupply) / (10 ** asset.decimals); // => 10,000.00 MLOFT // 2. Converting valuation_cents (USD cents to USD dollars): // Given valuation_cents = "500000000": const rawCents = BigInt(asset.valuation_cents); const displayUsd = Number(rawCents) / 100; // => 5000000.00 ($5,000,000.00 USD)

title: API · Filtering and sorting assets
description: Filter and sort the asset list server-side.
content: Filtering and sorting assets GET /v1/assets accepts these query parameters: Parameter Values Description asset_type e.g. real_estate Only assets of this class. active true , false Only active or inactive assets. sort valuation Sort by USD valuation (ordered by valuation_cents in USD cents). order asc , desc (default) Direction; requires sort . offset , limit integers Pagination (limit defaults to 50, max 100). curl "$API_BASE_URL/v1/assets?asset_type=real_estate&sort=valuation&order=asc" Invalid or unknown parameters return 400 with a body of the form {"error": "invalid_parameter", "message": "..."} .

title: API · Compliance
description: Non-PII compliance summary for a tokenized asset.
content: Compliance Replace $API_BASE_URL in examples with your configured API base URL (see API Overview ). Returns an aggregate view of an asset's KYC allowlist. It deliberately exposes counts, not addresses — no personally identifying information leaves the API. Path parameters Name Type Notes id number Registry id Response schema Field Type Notes total_records number Addresses ever added to the allowlist approved number Stored KYC status is Approved — not the same as currently passing is_allowed suspended number rejected number pending number with_expiry number Records with a non-zero expires_at jurisdictions array { jurisdiction, count } breakdown Example curl $API_BASE_URL/assets/1/compliance { "total_records": 1, "approved": 1, "suspended": 0, "rejected": 0, "pending": 0, "with_expiry": 0, "jurisdictions": [ { "jurisdiction": "US", "count": 1 } ] } Errors Returns 404 with { "error": "not_found", … } when the asset id is unknown. An asset's holder set can itself be sensitive. This endpoint gives issuers and analysts the shape of an allowlist — how many are approved, where they're based, how many approvals carry expiries — without publishing who they are. The per-address KYC records live only on-chain and in the issuer's own tooling. approved (and the other status counts) reflect each record's stored status field, not the on-chain is_allowed check the compliance contract actually enforces at transfer time. A record can be counted as approved here while is_allowed would reject it — for example an approval that has expired ( expires_at in the past) or one whose jurisdiction has since been blocked via is_jurisdiction_blocked . Use with_expiry together with the current time, and cross-reference jurisdictions against the contract's blocked-jurisdiction list, if you need a true count of holders currently permitted to transact. Do not treat approved as that number on its own. The jurisdictions breakdown reflects the jurisdiction field of each KYC record. Combined with the contract's is_jurisdiction_blocked , it helps issuers audit their geographic exposure. See the Compliance Guide .

title: API · Compliance › Address compliance
content: Returns the compliance authorization and token balance for an address across all assets it holds. curl "$API_BASE_URL/compliance/GAIQGTOBTTLLDJ4SWGGESM7UWJ2DI4K3ZNHUSHPDKJL2IE5FKY3BSRAA" [ { "address": "GAIQGTOBTTLLDJ4SWGGESM7UWJ2DI4K3ZNHUSHPDKJL2IE5FKY3BSRAA", "asset_id": 1, "asset_name": "Manhattan Loft", "symbol": "MLOFT", "balance": "1000000", "status": "approved", "allowed": true } ] Response schema (per record): Field Type Description address string Stellar account address asset_id number Registry asset id asset_name string Name of the asset symbol string Token symbol balance string Token balance in base units ( i128 string in the asset token's decimals base). Divide by 10 decimals to obtain human-readable units. status string Stored KYC status (e.g. approved , pending ) allowed boolean Current compliance authorization flag ( true if permitted to transact) // Balance is in base units; divide by 10 decimals (found in the asset's metadata): const displayBalance = Number(BigInt(record.balance)) / (10 ** decimals);

title: API · Dividends
description: Distribution history for a tokenized asset.
content: Dividends Replace $API_BASE_URL in examples with your configured API base URL (see API Overview ). Returns every dividend distribution created for the asset's token, ordered by creation ledger (newest first). Path parameters Name Type Notes id number Registry id Response schema (per distribution): Field Type Notes id number Distribution id asset_token string The asset paid out on payment_token string Token used to pay total_amount string Pool size in payment-token base units ( i128 string). Divide by 10 ** payment_token_decimals to get human-readable units. distributed string Claimed so far in payment-token base units ( i128 string). Divide by 10 ** payment_token_decimals to get human-readable units. claimed_percent number Percentage of pool claimed, 0–100 with 2 decimal places ( f64 ). overflow_detected boolean true when distributed exceeds total_amount (on-chain anomaly, not an API bug) completed boolean true once fully claimed created_at_ledger number Example curl $API_BASE_URL/assets/1/dividends [ { "id": 1, "asset_token": "CBMCWLSQSWUTLUJFCNBHNBSXMUM3XU7NAQ5TSNERW4HA4ZZBYHLG4ECZ", "payment_token": "CDLZFC3SYJYDZT7K67VZ75HPJVIEUVNIXF47ZG2FB2RMQQVU2HHGCYSC", "total_amount": "100000000000", "distributed": "25000000000", "claimed_percent": 25.0, "overflow_detected": false, "completed": false, "created_at_ledger": 3510000 } ] An asset with no distributions returns an empty array [] . Errors Returns 404 with { "error": "not_found", … } when the asset id is unknown.

title: API · Dividends › Get a single distribution
content: Path parameters Name Type Notes id number Registry id did number Distribution id Response schema Same shape as a single item from the list above. Example curl $API_BASE_URL/assets/1/distributions/1 { "id": 1, "asset_token": "CBMCWLSQSWUTLUJFCNBHNBSXMUM3XU7NAQ5TSNERW4HA4ZZBYHLG4ECZ", "payment_token": "CDLZFC3SYJYDZT7K67VZ75HPJVIEUVNIXF47ZG2FB2RMQQVU2HHGCYSC", "total_amount": "100000000000", "distributed": "25000000000", "claimed_percent": 25.0, "completed": false, "created_at_ledger": 3510000 } Errors Returns 404 with { "error": "not_found", … } when the asset id or the distribution id is unknown. total_amount and distributed are measured in the payment token's base units, not the asset token's. Classic Stellar assets (SACs) such as USDC use 7 decimals, whereas other tokens may specify different decimals. // Converting distribution amounts for a payment token with 7 decimals (e.g. SAC USDC): const paymentDecimals = 7; // Pool size: const rawTotal = BigInt(distribution.total_amount); // "100000000000" const displayTotal = Number(rawTotal) / (10 paymentDecimals); // => 10,000.0 USDC // Claimed so far: const rawDistributed = BigInt(distribution.distributed); // "25000000000" const displayDistributed = Number(rawDistributed) / (10 paymentDecimals); // => 2,500.0 USDC

title: API · Error Bodies
description: The single JSON error shape returned by every route of the Stellar RWA API, with the full list of error codes.
content: Error Bodies Every error response, from any route or from the server itself, has the same JSON shape and an application/json content type: { "error": "not_found", "message": "no asset with id 999" } Field Type Description error string Stable, machine-readable code. Branch on this. message string Human-readable explanation. Do not parse it. The body contains exactly these two fields. Headers such as Retry-After are preserved on the response.

title: API · Error Bodies › Error codes
content: HTTP status error When 400 bad_request Malformed query string or path parameter 401 unauthorized /metrics called without a valid bearer token 404 not_found Unknown asset, distribution or route 405 method_not_allowed Any method other than GET 408 request_timeout The request exceeded the server timeout 413 payload_too_large The request body exceeded the size limit 429 too_many_requests The per-IP rate limit was exceeded 500 internal_server_error Unexpected server error 503 service_unavailable The service cannot answer right now GET /health is a status report rather than an error: it returns its own JSON status document, with a 503 status while the snapshot is stale.

title: API · Events
description: Recent contract events emitted by the indexer.
content: Events The API exposes a compact event stream for clients that need to react to state changes without polling the full asset list. The payload is a JSON array ordered newest-first. curl "$API_BASE_URL/events?limit=20" [ { "id": 42, "contract": "CDL...", "event_type": "Transfer", "ledger": 3514152, "timestamp": "2026-07-09T08:43:12.101772791+00:00", "data": { "from": "GA...", "to": "GB...", "amount": "100" } } ] Each event includes the contract address, event name, ledger, timestamp (when available), and the raw payload emitted by the contract. Response schema: Field Type Description id number Sequential event ID contract string Address of the contract emitting the event event_type string Event name (e.g. Transfer , Mint , Burn , Valuation , created , claim ) ledger number Ledger sequence number where the event was recorded timestamp string or null ISO 8601 timestamp of ledger close data object Event-specific data payload Event payload amount units: Amounts inside data depend on the contract and event type, in accordance with the contracts specification: Event type Amount field Unit / Base Conversion Transfer , Mint , Burn data.amount Asset token base units ( i128 string) Number(BigInt(data.amount)) / 10 token.decimals Valuation data.new_valuation USD cents ( i128 string) Number(BigInt(data.new_valuation)) / 100 Dividend created data.total_amount Payment token base units ( i128 string) Number(BigInt(data.total_amount)) / 10 payment_token.decimals Dividend claim data.amount Payment token base units ( i128 string) Number(BigInt(data.amount)) / 10 payment_token.decimals // For a Transfer event with amount = "100" and token decimals = 2: const rawAmount = BigInt(event.data.amount); const displayAmount = Number(rawAmount) / (10 2); // => 1.00 token

title: API · Field selection
description: Request partial responses with the fields parameter.
content: Field selection Every JSON data endpoint under /v1 (assets, holders, events, dividends and single-record endpoints) accepts ?fields= with a comma-separated list of field names. Each returned object then contains only those fields. curl "$API_BASE_URL/v1/assets?fields=id,symbol,valuation_usd" curl "$API_BASE_URL/v1/assets/1/holders?fields=address,balance" Requesting a field that does not exist returns 400 : {"error": "invalid_parameter", "message": "unknown field nope ; available fields: ..."} Fields are validated against the first record of a list, so an empty list is returned as-is. When selecting amount fields like balance , remember that values are returned in raw base units. If you plan to format the balance for display, include decimals in your field list (or query the parent asset) so you can convert balance / 10 ** decimals . Similarly, note that valuation_cents is in USD cents while valuation_usd is in USD dollars.

title: API · Health & Indexer Lag
description: How GET /health reports the last successful poll, ledger lag and staleness.
content: Health & indexer lag GET /health returns 200 with "status": "ok" while the indexer is polling normally, and 503 with "status": "degraded" when it has stalled. Field Meaning snapshot_age_seconds Age of the served snapshot last_poll_at Time of the last successful poll (RFC 3339) last_poll_age_seconds Seconds since the last successful poll last_indexed_ledger Ledger reached by the last successful poll ledger_lag Estimated ledgers closed since that poll (about 5 seconds each) max_age_seconds Stall threshold

title: API · Health & Indexer Lag › Threshold
content: The indexer is reported unhealthy when the last successful poll is older than max_age_seconds . The default is three poll intervals (30 seconds). Override it with the RWA_HEALTH_MAX_POLL_AGE_SECS environment variable.

title: API · Health & Indexer Lag › Staleness during an RPC outage
content: The indexer counts consecutive failed polls and reports the count as consecutive_failures in /health . While polls are failing, or the last successful poll is older than the threshold, every response carries: - X-Data-Stale: true - X-Data-Age-Seconds : seconds since the last successful poll - X-Indexer-Consecutive-Failures : current failure streak The previous snapshot keeps being served. When a poll succeeds again, the headers disappear and the recovery is logged.

title: API · Holder position
content: Holder position curl "$API_BASE_URL/v1/holders/$ADDRESS/position" { "address": "G...", "asset_count": 1, "total_value_usd": 50.0, "positions": [ { "asset_id": 1, "asset_name": "Test Asset", "symbol": "TST", "balance": "250", "share_percent": 25.0, "value_usd": 50.0, "claimable": [ { "distribution_id": 7, "payment_token": "C...", "amount": "200" } ] } ] } Response schema: Field Type Unit / Description address string Stellar account address asset_count number Count of assets held with a positive balance total_value_usd number Total estimated value across all held positions in USD dollars ( f64 ) positions array Array of asset position objects positions[].asset_id number Registry asset id positions[].asset_name string Name of the asset positions[].symbol string Token symbol positions[].balance string Holder's token balance in base units ( i128 string in the asset's decimals base). Divide by 10 ** decimals to obtain the token amount. positions[].share_percent number Share of the asset's total supply owned, 0–100 with 2 decimal places ( f64 ) positions[].value_usd number Estimated position value in USD dollars ( f64 ), calculated from share_percent of the asset's valuation positions[].claimable array Unclaimed pro-rata shares across open dividend distributions positions[].claimable[].distribution_id number Distribution identifier positions[].claimable[].payment_token string Contract address of the token used to pay the dividend positions[].claimable[].amount string Estimated claimable dividend in payment-token base units ( i128 string). Divide by 10 payment_decimals (e.g. 7 for SAC USDC). - value_usd is the holder's share_percent of the asset valuation. - claimable lists each open distribution with the holder's pro-rata share ( balance / total_supply ) of the unclaimed pool, in payment-token base units. It is an estimate from indexed data, not an on-chain claim quote. - An address with no holdings returns an empty positions array. Because asset tokens and payment tokens may use different decimal bases, always scale each amount using its corresponding token decimals: // 1. Convert asset token balance (e.g. TST with decimals = 2): const rawBalance = BigInt(position.balance); // "250" const assetDecimals = 2; const displayBalance = Number(rawBalance) / (10 assetDecimals); // => 2.50 TST // 2. Convert claimable dividend (e.g. USDC payment token with decimals = 7): const rawClaimable = BigInt(position.claimable[0].amount); // "200" const paymentDecimals = 7; const displayClaimable = Number(rawClaimable) / (10 ** paymentDecimals); // => 0.0000200 USDC

title: API · Holders
description: Holder list with balances for a tokenized asset.
content: Holders Replace $API_BASE_URL in examples with your configured API base URL (see API Overview ). Returns every address that is on the asset's compliance allowlist and holds a positive balance. The asset-token contract does not enumerate holders directly, so the indexer derives this from the allowlist intersected with balances. Path parameters Name Type Notes id number Registry id Query parameters (all optional) Name Type Notes offset integer Skip the first N holders. Default: 0 . limit integer Page size. Default: 50 ; maximum: 100 . Response schema (per holder): Field Type Notes address string Holder account balance string Balance in base units ( i128 string in the asset token's decimals base). Divide by 10 ** decimals (from the asset's metadata) to get the display balance. share_percent number Share of total token supply, 0–100 with 2 decimal places ( balance / total_supply * 100 ). Example curl $API_BASE_URL/assets/1/holders [ { "address": "GAIQGTOBTTLLDJ4SWGGESM7UWJ2DI4K3ZNHUSHPDKJL2IE5FKY3BSRAA", "balance": "1000000", "share_percent": 100.0 } ] Errors Returns 404 with { "error": "not_found", … } when the asset id is unknown. An asset with holders but none currently holding a positive balance returns an empty array [] . Holder balances are raw integers on-chain. To format a balance for end users, query the asset's decimals value and scale the integer: // Given holder.balance = "1000000" and asset.decimals = 2: const rawBalance = BigInt(holder.balance); const displayBalance = Number(rawBalance) / (10 ** asset.decimals); // => 10,000.00 tokens Holders are sorted by balance, largest first. share_percent is computed from balance / total_supply at index time, so it reflects the most recent 10-second refresh.

title: API · OpenAPI Specification
description: Machine-readable OpenAPI 3 specification covering every v1 route of the Stellar RWA API.
content: OpenAPI specification The v1 surface is described by an OpenAPI 3 document, served by the docs site at /openapi-v1.yaml . It lists / , /version , /health , /metrics and every route under /v1 , and can be fed to client generators or contract-testing tools. The spec source lives at docs/public/openapi-v1.yaml and is linted in CI by the OpenAPI workflow on every change.

title: API Overview
description: How the read-only Stellar RWA indexing API works, and its conventions.
content: API Overview The Stellar RWA API is a read-only REST service that indexes all tokenized asset activity on Stellar and serves it as JSON. It is written in Rust (Axum + tokio) and holds no keys — it never signs or submits transactions. Base URL: Set via environment variable NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL (defaults to http://localhost:8080 for development). Readers should replace examples with their configured URL. An OpenAPI 3.0 specification is available at /openapi.json — use it with Swagger UI, Postman, or to generate SDK clients. See Integration Guide for examples.

title: API Overview › Non-goals
content: The API is deliberately limited. It does not : - Hold keys. No secret key is configured or stored. The only account it knows about, RWA_READ_SOURCE , is a public address used as the unsigned source of simulated view calls. - Sign or submit transactions. Every contract read is a simulateTransaction envelope with an empty signature set that is never sent to the network. Every route is a GET ; there is no write endpoint. - Change on-chain state. Issuing, transferring, allowlisting and dividend claims all happen through the web app, signed by the user's wallet (see Integration Guide ). - Act as the source of truth. It is a ~10-second-old in-memory cache of the Soroban ledger, with no database. Trust implication: compromising the API cannot move funds, change an allowlist, or authorize anything on-chain — there is nothing to steal and no signing path to abuse. The worst a faulty or malicious API can do is serve stale or incorrect data, so verify anything security-critical against the ledger directly before acting on it. See Architecture for how this fits the wider system.

title: API Overview › How indexing works
content: A background task polls Soroban RPC every 10 seconds. On each tick it reads the current state of the four contracts by simulating view calls — get_all_assets on the registry, then per-asset get_metadata , get_allowlist , balance and get_distributions_for_asset — and rebuilds an in-memory snapshot. For the full polling model and what it means for data freshness, see How the indexer rebuilds state . State is kept in memory (no database in v1). If the RPC is briefly unreachable, the indexer logs the error, keeps serving the last good snapshot, and retries on the next tick. The API never panics on a transient failure.

title: API Overview › Authentication and rate limiting
content: There is currently no authentication required to call the data endpoints (everything under /v1 , plus / , /version and /health ). The one exception is the operator-only /metrics endpoint, which requires a bearer token. The API applies request throttling, and its /v1 data routes support HTTP caching with Cache-Control and ETags. The X-RateLimit-* response headers described in the reference are planned; caching is already available: See Rate Limits & Caching for the active ETag conditional-request flow and cache headers, along with the planned rate-limit response headers and polling recommendations.

title: API Overview › Data freshness and caching
content: The API refreshes its in-memory state approximately every 10 seconds by polling Soroban RPC. This means: - Data lags the ledger by ~10 seconds on average. - Two requests made within the same 10-second window will return identical data. - If Soroban RPC is temporarily unreachable, the API continues serving the last successful snapshot (no error, just stale data). For integrations where you need real-time data, consider reading contracts directly via Soroban RPC.

title: API Overview › Metrics endpoint
content: GET /metrics exposes indexer health in the Prometheus text exposition format ( Content-Type: text/plain; version=0.0.4 ). It is intended for operators, not API consumers, and is not part of the /v1 namespace or its stability promise. Authentication The endpoint is protected by a static bearer token configured on the server: Environment variable Purpose RWA_METRICS_TOKEN Shared secret that scrapers must present. Scrapers send it in the Authorization header: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $RWA_METRICS_TOKEN" http://localhost:8080/metrics - The header must be exactly Bearer ; the token is compared verbatim. - A missing, malformed or wrong token returns 401 Unauthorized with the plain text body metrics authentication required . - If RWA_METRICS_TOKEN is unset or empty , the endpoint is disabled and every request returns 401 . There is no way to expose metrics without a token. - The variable is read on every request, but since it comes from the process environment, rotating it means restarting the API with the new value. Treat RWA_METRICS_TOKEN like any other secret: generate a long random value (for example openssl rand -hex 32 ), keep it out of source control, and serve the API over TLS so the token is not sent in clear text. Exposed metrics Metric Type Labels Description rwa_indexer_refresh_duration_seconds summary — Wall-clock time of each indexer refresh (one sample per poll tick, successful or not). Rendered with quantile series plus _sum and _count . rwa_indexer_refresh_total counter outcome = success \ failure Number of completed refresh attempts. A failure means the whole tick failed and the previous snapshot kept being served. rwa_indexer_asset_read_errors_total counter asset_id , read = get_metadata \ compliance \ dividends \ dividend_decode Per-asset RPC reads that failed during an otherwise successful refresh. Series only appear after they are first recorded, so a freshly started API may return an empty body until the first refresh completes, and rwa_indexer_asset_read_errors_total is absent until a read actually fails. Useful alert starting points: Refreshes are failing rate(rwa_indexer_refresh_total{outcome="failure"}[5m]) > 0 No successful refresh in the last minute (normal cadence is ~10s) increase(rwa_indexer_refresh_total{outcome="success"}[1m]) == 0 A specific asset keeps failing to read increase(rwa_indexer_asset_read_errors_total[15m]) > 0 For snapshot age, use GET /health , which returns 503 with "status": "degraded" once the snapshot is older than three poll intervals. Example scrape configuration Store the token in a file readable by Prometheus and reference it with credentials_file , so it never appears in the config itself: scrape_configs: - job_name: stellar-rwa-api scrape_interval: 15s metrics_path: /metrics scheme: https authorization: type: Bearer credentials_file: /etc/prometheus/secrets/rwa-metrics-token static_configs: - targets: ["rwa-api.example.com"] A scrape interval of 10–15 seconds matches the indexer's poll cadence; scraping faster does not yield new data.

title: API Overview › Versioning and stability
content: All data endpoints are served under the /v1 prefix (for example GET /v1/assets/:id ). The path prefix is the compatibility contract: a client written against /v1 should keep working, unmodified, for as long as /v1 is served. GET /version returns the running server version so clients can log or report it, but clients should not need to branch on it.

title: API Overview › What /v1 covers
content: The stability promise applies to every route under /v1 , including its path and query parameters, response JSON shapes, field types and meanings, HTTP status codes, and the error body format and error codes. It does not cover operator-facing routes ( /metrics , /health , / ), the exact values of rate-limit budgets, the indexing interval, or anything marked as experimental or planned in these docs.

title: API Overview › Changes that may ship without a version bump
description: Changes that may ship without a version bump
content: These are additive or behavioural changes that a well-behaved client already tolerates. Clients must ignore unknown fields and unknown enum values to benefit from them. - Adding new endpoints under /v1 . - Adding new optional query parameters with a default that preserves the current behaviour. - Adding new fields to response objects. - Adding new values to open-ended string enums (for example a new event type or a new error code for a previously unhandled case). - Adding new response headers. - Changing the wording of human-readable message strings. - Changing ordering where the order is not documented as guaranteed. - Tuning operational limits (rate limits, timeouts, body size, poll interval) and fixing bugs so behaviour matches the documentation.

title: API Overview › Changes that require a new version
description: Changes that require a new version
content: These are breaking and will only ship under a new prefix ( /v2 ): - Removing or renaming an endpoint, field, or query parameter. - Changing a field's type or encoding (for example turning a decimal string such as total_supply into a number) or its units (for example cents to dollars). - Making an optional parameter required, or changing a default in a way that alters results. - Changing the status code or error code returned for an existing condition. - Changing the meaning of an existing field or the semantics of an endpoint. - Changing pagination, ETag, or error-body structure.

title: API Overview › Deprecation policy
content: - When /v2 is introduced, /v1 keeps running alongside it; the two are served from the same process and index. - A deprecation is announced in these docs and the changelog before anything is removed, and /v1 remains available for at least 6 months after /v2 is generally available. - Individual /v1 fields or endpoints may be marked deprecated in the docs and the OpenAPI spec ( deprecated: true ) ahead of time, but are not removed from /v1 itself. - Security fixes may change behaviour without notice when there is no compatible alternative; such changes will be called out in the changelog.

title: API Overview › Amount units and conventions
content: All monetary amounts and token supplies in the API reference adhere to strict unit rules that agree with the underlying Soroban contracts: - Large integers are strings. Token amounts, valuations, balances, and dividend pools are 128-bit signed integers ( i128 ) on-chain. To eliminate precision loss in JavaScript and other IEEE 754 floating-point runtimes, they are serialized as decimal strings ( total_supply , valuation_cents , tvl_cents , balance , total_amount , distributed ). - Valuations are USD cents. valuation_cents (on assets) and tvl_cents (on stats) represent valuations in USD cents ( 1 USD = 100 cents ). To convert to dollar display values, divide by 100: `` typescript const cents = BigInt(asset.valuation_cents); // "500000000" const dollars = Number(cents) / 100; // 5000000.00 ($5,000,000.00) ` - Convenience floats. For quick display and charting, valuations also provide a valuation_usd and tvl_usd ( f64 US dollars), and percentages are given as numbers ( share_percent , claimed_percent ). - Token amounts are in the token's own decimals base. Asset balances ( balance ) and supplies ( total_supply ) are given as raw integer base units. Divide by 10 decimals (where decimals is the asset's configured decimal places, e.g. 2 or 7 ): ` typescript const rawSupply = BigInt(asset.total_supply); // "1000000" const displaySupply = Number(rawSupply) / (10 asset.decimals); // 10000.00 ` - Dividend pools use payment-token base units. In dividend distributions, total_amount , distributed , and claimable shares are measured in base units of the payment token (e.g. Classic Stellar assets / SAC tokens like USDC typically use 7 decimals): ` typescript const rawDividend = BigInt(distribution.total_amount); // "100000000000" const paymentDecimals = 7; const displayDividend = Number(rawDividend) / (10 paymentDecimals); // 10000.0 USDC ` Amount field Format Unit Conversion to display valuation_cents string ( i128 ) USD cents Number(BigInt(valuation_cents)) / 100 valuation_usd number ( f64 ) USD dollars Already in USD tvl_cents string ( i128 ) USD cents Number(BigInt(tvl_cents)) / 100 tvl_usd number ( f64 ) USD dollars Already in USD total_supply string ( i128 ) Asset token base units Number(BigInt(total_supply)) / 10 decimals balance string ( i128 ) Asset token base units Number(BigInt(balance)) / 10 decimals total_amount string ( i128 ) Payment token base units Number(BigInt(total_amount)) / 10 payment_decimals distributed string ( i128 ) Payment token base units Number(BigInt(distributed)) / 10 ** payment_decimals`

title: API Overview › Error responses
content: The response body depends on where an error is generated. Resource-not-found errors use the API's JSON format: { "error": "not_found", "message": "no asset with id 999" } For this API-generated JSON body, error is a machine-readable code and message is a human-readable explanation. Request-extraction failures and middleware errors are generated by the HTTP framework and may instead return plain text. Branch on the HTTP status; do not assume every failure uses the JSON shape above. Common errors: HTTP status Body format Meaning 400 Bad Request Plain-text diagnostic A path parameter or query value cannot be parsed, such as a non-numeric asset :id or malformed pagination value. 401 Unauthorized Plain text /metrics was called without a valid bearer token. 404 Not Found JSON {"error":"not_found","message":"..."} for a missing resource The requested asset or distribution does not exist. An unknown URL may use the framework's not-found response instead. 429 Too Many Requests Plain-text throttle message The per-IP rate limit was exceeded. See Rate Limits & Caching for the response and backoff guidance. 500 Internal Server Error Not a stable API error shape An unexpected server failure occurred. Treat the body as diagnostic and report persistent failures. 503 Service Unavailable JSON health status GET /health reports degraded when the indexed snapshot is too old. The body includes snapshot_age_seconds and max_age_seconds . Only the resource-not-found JSON body is a stable API error schema today. The plain-text framework and middleware messages are useful for debugging, but clients should not parse them to decide how to handle a failure.

Divide by 100 for USD dollars. tvl_usd number Total value locked in USD dollars ( f64 float convenience field, equal to tvl_cents / 100 ) total_holders number Count of distinct approved addresses with a positive balance across all assets total_distributions number Total dividend distributions created across all assets last_indexed_ledger number Most recent ledger read by the indexer last_updated string or null RFC 3339 timestamp of the last successful index refresh total_holders is the count of distinct approved addresses across all assets; last_indexed_ledger is the ledger the most recent successful refresh read from.

title: API · Rate Limits & Caching
description: Rate-limit headers, ETag-based conditional requests, and Cache-Control guidance for the Stellar RWA API.
content: Rate Limits & Caching Rate limiting is keyed by client IP and uses a token bucket shared across API routes. Conditional requests are enabled on the /v1 data routes.

title: API · Rate Limits & Caching › Rate limits
content: The default sustained rate is 5 requests per second per client IP , with a maximum burst of 20 requests . Tokens refill at one every 200 ms; this is a token bucket, not a fixed one-minute window. The limit is shared across API routes and can be changed with RWA_RATE_LIMIT_PER_SECOND and RWA_RATE_LIMIT_BURST .

title: API · Rate Limits & Caching › When the limit is exceeded
content: When a request arrives before a token is available, the API responds with HTTP 429 Too Many Requests . The default middleware response is plain text, not the API's JSON error format: HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests Too Many Requests! Wait for s The number of seconds varies with the time until the next token is available. The API does not currently send Retry-After or X-RateLimit-* headers. On 429 , pause for at least the indicated number of seconds when present, with a minimum one-second delay. Otherwise, use exponential backoff with jitter (and cap the delay), and retry only idempotent requests. For polling use cases, the indexer refreshes its state about every 10 seconds, so polling more frequently does not provide fresher data. Use a 10–15 second polling interval and back off promptly after a 429 .

title: API · Rate Limits & Caching › HTTP caching with ETags
content: Snapshot-backed /v1 data endpoints return a strong ETag derived from the latest indexed ledger, along with Cache-Control: public, max-age=10 . /health and other non-data routes do not return these cache headers.

title: API · Rate Limits & Caching › How it works
content: 1. Make a normal request — the response includes an ETag header. 2. On the next request, send the value back in If-None-Match . 3. If the snapshot has not changed, the server returns 304 Not Modified with an empty body, saving bandwidth. The request still counts toward the rate limit. 4. If the snapshot has changed, the server returns 200 OK with the new body and a new ETag . First request — capture the ETag API_BASE_URL includes /v1, for example http://localhost:8080/v1 curl -i "$API_BASE_URL/assets/1" HTTP/1.1 200 OK ETag: "ledger-3514152" Cache-Control: public, max-age=10 Second request — send the ETag back curl -i -H 'If-None-Match: "ledger-3514152"' "$API_BASE_URL/assets/1" HTTP/1.1 304 Not Modified (empty body)

title: API · Rate Limits & Caching › TypeScript helper
content: const API = process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL ?? "http://localhost:8080/v1"; const etagCache = new Map (); const url = ${API}${path} ; const cached = etagCache.get(url); const headers: HeadersInit = cached ? { "If-None-Match": cached.etag } : {}; const res = await fetch(url, { headers }); if (res.status === 304 && cached) { // Server confirmed nothing changed — reuse the cached body. return cached.data as T; } if (!res.ok) throw new Error( API ${res.status} ); const data = (await res.json()) as T; const etag = res.headers.get("ETag"); if (etag) etagCache.set(url, { etag, data }); return data; }

title: API · Rate Limits & Caching › Which endpoints support ETags?
content: All snapshot-backed /v1 read endpoints support ETags. The /health endpoint does not return an ETag because liveness probes should always get a fresh response. Endpoint ETag GET /stats ✅ GET /events ✅ GET /assets ✅ GET /assets/:id ✅ GET /assets/:id/holders ✅ GET /assets/:id/compliance ✅ GET /assets/:id/dividends ✅ GET /assets/:id/distributions/:did ✅ GET /holders/:address ✅ GET /holders/:address/compliance ✅ GET /compliance/:address ✅ GET /health ❌

title: API · Rate Limits & Caching › Cache-Control
content: The API sets Cache-Control: public, max-age=10 on snapshot-backed responses, matching the indexer's approximately 10-second refresh interval. If you are fronting the API with a CDN, configure it to forward the If-None-Match / ETag headers so conditional requests reach the origin rather than being absorbed by the CDN's own cache.

title: API · Rate Limits & Caching › Recommendations for integrators
content: - Poll at the refresh interval. The indexer rebuilds state every ~10 seconds. Polling more frequently wastes budget without gaining fresher data. A 10–15 s interval is a good default. - Use ETags for asset detail pages. Asset metadata rarely changes. Send If-None-Match on every poll — most responses will be 304 . - Handle 429 responses. Back off with jitter; the API does not expose a remaining-request counter. - Cache locally for read-heavy UIs. If your frontend renders the same data across multiple components, fetch once and share the result rather than making one request per component. - Prefer the API over direct Soroban RPC for display data. The API reduces the number of outbound RPC calls your integration makes and returns pre-decoded JSON. Use direct RPC only when you need live data that has not been indexed yet.

title: API · Request IDs & Logging
description: Correlate a response with server logs using the request id.
content: Request IDs & logging Every response carries an X-Request-Id header. Send your own X-Request-Id (up to 64 characters of letters, digits, - and _ ) to have it reused. JSON error bodies include the same value as request_id : { "error": "not_found", "message": "Asset 7 not found", "request_id": "3f9a1c0b7d2e4a86" } The server logs one structured line per request inside a span carrying request_id , method and path , with status , latency_ms , indexed_ledger and consecutive_failures , so a report can be matched to the indexer state at that moment. Set RUST_LOG to control verbosity.

title: Architecture Overview › Repository ownership
content: Repository Language / stack Owns Open to contributors? stellar-rwa-contracts Rust · Soroban SDK The four on-chain programs; all business logic and compliance rules Maintainer-only stellar-rwa-api-docs — api/ Rust · Axum · tokio Read-only indexer; polls Soroban RPC, caches state in memory, serves JSON Maintainer-only stellar-rwa-api-docs — docs/ Next.js 14 · MDX This documentation site Open — see CONTRIBUTING.md stellar-rwa-web Next.js · Freighter API Issuer and investor front-end; the only layer that signs transactions Maintainer-only

title: Architecture Overview › How data flows
content: Writes (user → chain) 1. A user opens the web app and connects Freighter. 2. The web app builds a Soroban transaction and asks Freighter to sign it. 3. The signed transaction is submitted to Soroban RPC and lands on the ledger. 4. The contract executes — e.g., an asset-token transfer triggers a cross-contract is_allowed check in the compliance contract. Reads (chain → API → web app) 1. The API's background indexer calls simulateTransaction on Soroban RPC every 10 seconds, decoding the returned ScVal with stellar-xdr . 2. The decoded state is held in an in-memory snapshot (no database in v1). 3. The web app — and any other client — fetches that snapshot over REST. This is cheaper and simpler than every client simulating its own contract calls. The API is a read-only cache , not the source of truth. The Soroban ledger is. If you need data fresher than ~10 seconds, simulate the relevant view call directly with the Stellar JS SDK — see the Integration Guide .

title: Architecture Overview › How the indexer rebuilds state
content: The indexer does not replay contract events to derive state. On every cycle it re-reads the current contract state through simulated view calls and builds a brand-new snapshot from scratch. The polling model 1. Every 10 seconds ( POLL_INTERVAL in api/src/indexer/mod.rs ) a background task starts a refresh cycle. 2. It calls get_all_assets on the registry , then for each asset reads get_metadata on the asset-token , the allowlist and balances via the compliance contract, and get_distributions_for_asset on the dividend contract. 3. The results are assembled into a new snapshot (assets, holders, compliance summaries, dividends and /stats ) and swapped in atomically. Readers see either the old snapshot or the new one — never a half-built mix. 4. Individual reads retry transient RPC errors in place with short backoff. If the cycle still fails, the previous snapshot keeps being served and the next attempt waits one poll interval (or the RPC's Retry-After , if it sent one). Because each cycle is a full re-read, there is no event cursor to fall behind and no replay after a restart: a freshly started API is empty until its first successful cycle, then fully current. Freshness implications - Lag. Snapshot data trails the ledger by up to one poll interval plus the time the cycle takes. last_indexed_ledger and last_updated on /stats tell you which ledger and when. - Dividends lag more. Distribution lists are cached per asset for 60 seconds inside the indexer, so a new or claimed distribution can take up to ~60 seconds to appear. - Partial staleness. If a single asset's reads fail, that asset keeps its previous data and carries an index_error , while the rest of the snapshot updates normally. Treat an asset with index_error as possibly stale. - HTTP caching. Snapshot-backed responses carry Cache-Control: public, max-age=10 and an ETag derived from last_indexed_ledger , so polling faster than every 10 seconds only returns the same data (or a 304 ). See Rate Limits & Caching . - In-memory only. Nothing is persisted; a restart discards the snapshot and the indexer rebuilds it on the next cycle.

title: Architecture Overview › Contracts on Stellar
content: There are four Soroban contracts, each with a distinct responsibility: Contract Responsibility asset-token Fungible token (SEP-41) with compliance gating. One instance per RWA. compliance Per-asset allowlist, KYC records, jurisdiction rules, expiry. registry Global index of all tokenized assets on the platform. dividend Escrows and distributes payment-token dividends to token holders. asset-token and compliance are always deployed as a pair — each asset-token holds the address of its compliance contract and calls is_allowed on every transfer. The registry and dividend contracts are platform-wide singletons . See the Contract Reference for full method signatures.

title: Architecture Overview › What the API does and does not do
description: What the API does and does not do
content: Does Does not Poll Soroban RPC and cache the result Hold private keys Serve plain JSON over REST Sign or submit transactions Decode XDR ScVal from contract view calls Store data persistently (in-memory only) Provide aggregated stats (TVL, holder counts) Enforce any access control beyond rate limiting Because the API never holds keys or submits transactions, it has a minimal attack surface. All write operations go through the web app → Freighter → Soroban RPC path, where the user's wallet is the only key holder.

title: Architecture Overview › Interface contracts
content: The three layers communicate through two stable interfaces: - Soroban contract ABI — the method names and ScVal types exposed by the four contracts. The API's indexer/mod.rs and the web app's SDK calls both depend on this. - REST API schema — the JSON shapes documented in the API Reference . The web app fetches from these endpoints; you can too. Changes to either interface are versioned. The API currently has no URL versioning (all paths are /... ); a v2 prefix will be added when breaking changes are needed.

title: Compliance Guide
description: The core of an RWA platform — allowlists, transfer gating, jurisdictions, KYC expiry.
content: Compliance Guide Compliance is what separates a real-world asset platform from a plain token factory. Anyone can mint a token; the hard part — and the regulated part — is controlling who is allowed to hold it . This guide explains the compliance model end to end: why it exists, how the allowlist works, how the on-chain transfer gate is enforced, and how issuers should operate it.

title: Compliance Guide › Why compliance matters for RWA
content: A real-world asset — equity in a building, a trade invoice, a warehouse of copper — is almost always a regulated instrument . The law in most jurisdictions restricts who may own it: accredited investors only, residents of permitted countries only, parties who have cleared KYC/AML checks only. If those restrictions live only in a web app, they are worthless — anyone can call the contract directly and bypass the UI. For a token to credibly represent a regulated asset, the restriction must be enforced by the asset itself , at the protocol level, on every transfer. That is exactly what this platform does. An RWA token can only ever be held by an address the issuer has explicitly approved — and the token enforces that on-chain, on every single transfer, by asking a separate compliance contract for permission.

title: Compliance Guide › How the allowlist model works
content: The compliance contract maintains a KYC allowlist : a set of KycRecord s, one per address. Each record carries: - a status — Approved , Pending , Rejected , or Suspended - a jurisdiction — an ISO country code ( US , KE , DE , …) - a verified_at ledger and an expires_at ledger ( 0 = never expires) Only the compliance admin (the issuer or their compliance officer) can change the allowlist, via add_to_allowlist , suspend , and remove . Adding an address sets its status to Approved ; suspending flips it to Suspended but keeps the record for audit; removing deletes it entirely. An address is permitted to hold or receive the asset only if is_allowed returns true , which requires all three of: 1. status is Approved , 2. the approval has not expired, and 3. the address's jurisdiction is not blocked.

title: Compliance Guide › How transfer gating works
content: This is the mechanism that makes the whole thing enforceable. The asset-token contract does not trust any off-chain system; on every transfer it makes cross-contract calls into the compliance contract for both parties: transfer(from, to, amount) ├─ from.require_auth() ├─ assert !paused ├─ compliance.is_allowed(from) ── cross-contract call ──▶ compliance contract ├─ compliance.is_allowed(to) ── cross-contract call ──▶ compliance contract └─ move balances + emit event If either is_allowed returns false , the transaction reverts — no balance moves, no event is emitted, the transfer simply cannot happen. The same check gates mint on the recipient, so tokens can never be minted into a non-approved wallet in the first place. Because the asset token depends only on the compliance interface ( is_allowed ), the concrete compliance contract can be swapped with set_compliance — for example to migrate to a stricter policy — without redeploying the token. Try to transfer the sample asset to an address that isn't on the allowlist. The transaction fails with RecipientNotCompliant (8) . That failure is the product working — the gate is doing its job.

title: Compliance Guide › What a failed gate looks like
description: What a failed gate looks like
content: Contract error Meaning SenderNotCompliant (7) The from address failed is_allowed RecipientNotCompliant (8) The to address failed is_allowed Paused (6) Transfers are globally halted by the issuer

title: Compliance Guide › Jurisdiction restrictions
content: Beyond per-address control, issuers can block entire jurisdictions . Calling block_jurisdiction("US") makes every approved address whose record says US fail is_allowed immediately — without editing a single individual record. Unblocking with unblock_jurisdiction("US") restores them. This models a common real-world requirement: a regulatory change, sanction, or offering restriction that must apply to a whole country at once. Because the check happens inside is_allowed at read time, the effect is instantaneous and retroactive — there is no list to re-scan and no window where stale approvals still work. The API's /assets/:id/compliance endpoint surfaces the jurisdiction distribution (as counts) so issuers can audit their geographic exposure before making such a change.

title: Compliance Guide › KYC expiry and suspension
content: Approvals are not forever. Two mechanisms let issuers keep the allowlist current: - Expiry. add_to_allowlist takes an expires_at ledger. Once the current ledger reaches it, is_allowed returns false automatically — the holder can no longer transfer, and cannot receive more, until re-approved. An expires_at of 0 means the approval never expires. Because time is measured in ledger sequence numbers (~5 seconds each), a one-year approval is roughly +6,300,000 ledgers from now. - Suspension. suspend(address) sets the status to Suspended while keeping the record. This is the right tool for a temporary hold — a pending re-review, a compliance flag — because it is reversible with add_to_allowlist and preserves the audit trail. Use remove only when an address should be erased entirely. There is no background job expiring records. The check is evaluated live against the current ledger every time is_allowed runs. An approval that lapsed one second ago fails the very next transfer — no cron, no lag.

title: Compliance Guide › Worked scenarios
content: These examples show how the live is_allowed gate affects a transfer. A transfer checks both the sender and recipient, so the error identifies which side failed. Scenario What the issuer or integrator sees Outcome and next step Unapproved recipient An address has no allowlist record, or its status is Pending or Rejected . is_allowed(recipient) returns false . The transfer reverts with RecipientNotCompliant (8) . Complete verification, then approve the recipient with add_to_allowlist ; retry only after the approval is in effect. Expired approval The record still says Approved , but the current ledger has reached expires_at . is_allowed returns false , and an outgoing transfer fails with SenderNotCompliant (7) ; an incoming transfer fails with RecipientNotCompliant (8) . Re-verify the holder and issue a new approval with a future expiry. Suspended holder The holder's record is retained for the audit trail but has status Suspended . is_allowed returns false . The holder cannot send ( SenderNotCompliant (7) ) or receive ( RecipientNotCompliant (8) ) until the compliance admin resolves the review and approves them again. Blocked jurisdiction The address has an otherwise valid approval, but its recorded jurisdiction is currently blocked. The jurisdiction check makes is_allowed return false immediately. Transfers from that holder fail with SenderNotCompliant (7) and transfers to them fail with RecipientNotCompliant (8) . Review the restriction before unblocking the jurisdiction or changing an individual's record. In all four cases, an off-chain status display is not a substitute for the contract check: use is_allowed for the asset's current compliance contract before submitting a transfer. The transaction itself remains authoritative and will revert if either party fails the gate.

title: Compliance Guide › Best practices for issuers
content: 1. Secure the compliance admin key. It is the single most powerful key in the system — it decides who can hold your asset. Use multisig and hardware custody. 2. Prefer suspend over remove . Suspension is reversible and preserves the record for audits; removal is destructive. 3. Set sensible expiries. Time-bounded approvals force periodic re-KYC and keep your allowlist from silently drifting out of date. Choose an expiry that matches your re-verification cadence. 4. Approve the issuer first. The asset token mints the initial supply to the admin, so the admin must be approved on the compliance contract before initialize , or deployment fails with RecipientNotCompliant . 5. Coordinate distributions with balances. The dividend contract reads balances at claim time. If you need a clean snapshot, consider pausing the token around a distribution window. See the Dividend contract . 6. Use jurisdiction blocks deliberately. They are immediate and affect every holder in the region. Review the jurisdiction breakdown from the API first. 7. Treat registry listing as self-attestation. Anyone can register an asset; the binding control is the compliance contract, not the registry entry.

title: Compliance Guide › Putting it together
content: The compliance contract is small, but it is the reason this platform can represent regulated assets at all. Every other piece — the token, the registry, the dividend escrow, the API, the web app — is built around the single invariant it enforces: > Only KYC-approved, unexpired, non-blocked addresses can ever hold the asset, > and the asset enforces this itself on every transfer. Next, see how issuers operate this in practice in the Web App Guide , or how to read compliance state programmatically in the Integration Guide .
