content: fn transfer(env: Env, from: Address, to: Address, amount: i128) Moves amount from from to to . Both parties must be compliance-approved and the token must not be paused. - Auth: from - Errors: InvalidAmount (5) if amount transfer performs two cross-contract calls into the compliance contract — is_allowed(from) and is_allowed(to) — before touching balances. This is the on-chain transfer gate. See How transfer gating works .

title: Asset Token Contract › mint
content: fn mint(env: Env, admin: Address, to: Address, amount: i128) Mints new tokens to a compliance-approved recipient, increasing total_supply . - Auth: admin (must equal the stored admin) - Errors: Unauthorized (3) , InvalidAmount (5) , Paused (6) , RecipientNotCompliant (8) , Overflow (9) .

title: Asset Token Contract › burn
content: fn burn(env: Env, from: Address, amount: i128) Burns amount of the caller's own tokens, decreasing total_supply . - Auth: from - Errors: InvalidAmount (5) , InsufficientBalance (4) .

title: Asset Token Contract › balance / total_supply
content: fn balance(env: Env, id: Address) -> i128 fn total_supply(env: Env) -> i128 View functions. balance returns 0 for an unknown address.

title: Asset Token Contract › pause / unpause
content: fn pause(env: Env, admin: Address) fn unpause(env: Env, admin: Address) Halts or resumes all transfers and mints. Auth: admin . Errors: Unauthorized (3) .

title: Asset Token Contract › update_valuation
content: fn update_valuation(env: Env, admin: Address, new_valuation: i128) Updates the recorded USD-cents valuation. Auth: admin . Errors: Unauthorized (3) , InvalidAmount (5) if negative.

title: Asset Token Contract › set_compliance
content: fn set_compliance(env: Env, admin: Address, compliance: Address) Points the token at a different compliance contract. Because the token knows only the compliance interface ( is_allowed ), the concrete contract can be swapped. Auth: admin .

title: Asset Token Contract › get_metadata
content: fn get_metadata(env: Env) -> AssetMetadata Returns the full metadata record.

title: Asset Token Contract › Code example
content: Transfer with the JS SDK, going through the compliance gate: const token = new Contract("CBMCWLSQ…4ECZ"); const op = token.call( "transfer", new Address(from).toScVal(), new Address(to).toScVal(), nativeToScVal(10000n, { type: "i128" }), // 100.00 @ 2 decimals ); // build → simulate → sign with Freighter → submit

title: Asset Token Contract › Events
content: Topic Data Emitted by ("mint", admin) total_supply initialize (initial mint) ("mint", to) amount mint ("transfer", from, to) amount transfer ("burn", from) amount burn ("pause",) / ("unpause",) admin pause / unpause ("valuation",) new_valuation update_valuation ("setcomp",) compliance set_compliance

title: Asset Token Contract › Security considerations
content: - Admin is fully trusted for minting, pausing, valuation and swapping the compliance contract. Use a secure key or multisig for the admin account. - Gate coupling: transfers depend on the compliance contract being live and correct. set_compliance is powerful — pointing at a permissive contract would disable the gate. Restrict admin access accordingly. - Integer amounts: all amounts are integers in the token's decimals base; there is no floating point. Reject amount <= 0 (the contract does). - Pause is a kill-switch: while paused, no value can move. This is intentional for incident response and regulatory holds.

title: Compliance Contract
description: KYC allowlist and jurisdiction rules — the on-chain transfer gate.
content: Compliance Contract Maintains the KYC allowlist and jurisdiction rules that gate who may hold or transfer a tokenized asset. The asset-token contract calls is_allowed on every transfer (for both sender and recipient) and on every mint (for the recipient). Time is expressed in ledger sequence numbers ( u32 ), not wall-clock dates. An expires_at of 0 means the approval never expires. Testnet: CBUERYDM7DXTZLLKDBRJKUBPFJ7M4OSUN4T7XKUARU345RLXNAIQD2IU

title: Compliance Contract › Data types
content: ComplianceStatus — Approved Pending Rejected Suspended . KycRecord : Field Type Notes address Address The KYC'd account status ComplianceStatus Only Approved passes the gate jurisdiction String ISO country code, e.g. US , KE , DE verified_at u32 Ledger at verification expires_at u32 Ledger of expiry; 0 = never

title: Compliance Contract › initialize
content: fn initialize(env: Env, admin: Address) Sets the admin. Callable once. Auth: admin . Errors: AlreadyInitialized (1) .

title: Compliance Contract › add_to_allowlist
content: fn add_to_allowlist( env: Env, admin: Address, address: Address, jurisdiction: String, expires_at: u32, ) Adds (or re-approves) an address, setting its status to Approved . If expires_at is non-zero it must be a future ledger. - Auth: admin - Errors: Unauthorized (5) , InvalidExpiry (4) if expires_at != 0 && expires_at <= now .

title: Compliance Contract › suspend
content: fn suspend(env: Env, admin: Address, address: Address) Sets an address's status to Suspended . The record is retained but is_allowed returns false until it is re-approved. Auth: admin . Errors: RecordNotFound (3) .

title: Compliance Contract › remove
content: fn remove(env: Env, admin: Address, address: Address) Deletes the record entirely and drops the address from the allowlist. Auth: admin . Errors: RecordNotFound (3) .

title: Compliance Contract › is_allowed
content: fn is_allowed(env: Env, address: Address) -> bool The core gate. Returns true only if the address is Approved , and not expired ( expires_at == 0 now Every check the RWA token performs funnels through is_allowed . Understanding its three conditions — status, expiry, jurisdiction — is understanding the whole compliance model. See the Compliance Guide .

title: Compliance Contract › get_record / get_allowlist
content: fn get_record(env: Env, address: Address) -> Option fn get_allowlist(env: Env) -> Vec get_record returns None for an unknown address. get_allowlist returns every address currently on the allowlist (any status except removed).

title: Compliance Contract › block_jurisdiction / unblock_jurisdiction / is_jurisdiction_blocked
content: fn block_jurisdiction(env: Env, admin: Address, jurisdiction: String) fn unblock_jurisdiction(env: Env, admin: Address, jurisdiction: String) fn is_jurisdiction_blocked(env: Env, jurisdiction: String) -> bool Blocking a jurisdiction makes every approved address in that jurisdiction fail is_allowed , without touching individual records. Auth: admin for the mutating calls.

title: Compliance Contract › Code example
content: Approve an investor in the US with a one-year expiry (~6.3M ledgers at 5s each): const compliance = new Contract("CBUERYDM…D2IU"); const op = compliance.call( "add_to_allowlist", new Address(admin).toScVal(), new Address(investor).toScVal(), nativeToScVal("US", { type: "string" }), nativeToScVal(currentLedger + 6_300_000, { type: "u32" }), );

title: Compliance Contract › Events
content: Topic Data Emitted by ("approved", address) (jurisdiction, expires_at) add_to_allowlist ("suspend", address) () suspend ("removed", address) () remove ("blockjur",) jurisdiction block_jurisdiction ("unblkjur",) jurisdiction unblock_jurisdiction

title: Compliance Contract › Security considerations
content: - Admin is the compliance authority. Whoever holds the admin key decides who can hold the asset. Protect it with multisig and clear operational controls. - Expiry is enforced at read time against the current ledger — an expired approval fails the gate immediately, with no cron job required. - Jurisdiction blocks are retroactive and immediate: blocking US instantly freezes every US holder's ability to transfer. Use deliberately. - remove vs suspend : suspend is reversible and keeps the audit record; remove erases it. Prefer suspend for temporary actions.

title: Dividend Contract
description: Proportional yield/dividend distribution to asset-token holders.
content: Dividend Contract Distributes yield/dividends to asset-token holders in proportion to their holdings. An issuer funds a distribution with a payment token; each holder then claims total_amount * balance / total_supply , paid from the escrow this contract holds. Each holder can claim a given distribution once. Balances are read at claim time from the asset token. Testnet: CAR4XY3CEBQWFOL27JEWFW34KXSIZA7RFKDQMEIV7ZU723RWY37I2SYX

title: Dividend Contract › Data types
content: Distribution : Field Type Notes id u64 Assigned sequentially asset_token Address The asset being paid out on payment_token Address The token used to pay (e.g. USDC) total_amount i128 Pool size in payment-token base units distributed i128 Claimed so far created_at u32 Ledger at creation completed bool true once fully claimed

title: Dividend Contract › initialize
content: fn initialize(env: Env, admin: Address) Sets the admin. Callable once. Auth: admin . Errors: AlreadyInitialized (1) .

title: Dividend Contract › create_distribution
content: fn create_distribution( env: Env, admin: Address, asset_token: Address, payment_token: Address, total_amount: i128, ) -> u64 Creates and funds a distribution, pulling total_amount of payment_token from the admin into the contract's escrow. Returns the distribution id. - Auth: admin (must equal the stored admin; the transfer also requires the admin's authorization) - Errors: Unauthorized (3) , InvalidAmount (5) if total_amount The admin must hold at least total_amount of the payment token and the transfer must succeed, or create_distribution reverts. Funds are escrowed in the dividend contract until claimed.

title: Dividend Contract › claimable
content: fn claimable(env: Env, distribution_id: u64, holder: Address) -> i128 Returns the amount a holder can still claim: 0 if already claimed, if they hold nothing, or if the distribution is empty. Otherwise total_amount * balance / total_supply (floored by integer division).

title: Dividend Contract › claim
content: fn claim(env: Env, distribution_id: u64, holder: Address) Pays the holder's proportional share from escrow and marks it claimed. - Auth: holder - Errors: DistributionNotFound (4) , AlreadyClaimed (7) , NothingToClaim (6) .

title: Dividend Contract › get_distribution / get_distributions_for_asset / has_claimed
content: fn get_distribution(env: Env, distribution_id: u64) -> Distribution fn get_distributions_for_asset(env: Env, asset_token: Address) -> Vec fn has_claimed(env: Env, distribution_id: u64, holder: Address) -> bool View helpers. get_distributions_for_asset backs the API's /assets/:id/dividends endpoint.

title: Dividend Contract › Code example
content: const dividend = new Contract("CAR4XY3C…2SYX"); // issuer funds a 10,000-unit distribution in the payment token const create = dividend.call( "create_distribution", new Address(admin).toScVal(), new Address(assetToken).toScVal(), new Address(paymentToken).toScVal(), nativeToScVal(10_000_0000000n, { type: "i128" }), // 10,000 @ 7 decimals ); // a holder later claims their share const claim = dividend.call( "claim", nativeToScVal(1n, { type: "u64" }), new Address(holder).toScVal(), );

title: Dividend Contract › Events
content: Topic Data Emitted by ("created", admin) (id, total_amount) create_distribution ("claim", holder) (distribution_id, amount) claim

title: Dividend Contract › Security considerations
content: - Balances are read at claim time , not at snapshot. A holder who acquires more tokens after a distribution is created — but before claiming — claims on the larger balance. Issuers should be aware of this when timing distributions, or pause the token around distribution windows. - Integer division floors each share, so a tiny residual may remain in escrow after everyone claims; completed flips once distributed >= total_amount . - Escrow custody: funds live in the dividend contract between creation and claim. The contract only pays out via claim ; there is no admin withdrawal path. - Payment-token decimals differ from the asset token. Amounts here are in the payment token's base units (7 for classic Stellar assets / SACs).

title: Registry Contract
description: Canonical on-chain index of every tokenized asset, plus total value locked.
content: Registry Contract A canonical, on-chain index of every tokenized asset on the platform. Each issuer registers their asset-token contract here; the registry assigns a monotonically increasing id and tracks issuer, type, valuation and active status. It also reports total value locked (TVL) across active assets. Testnet: CBX5SMLTXX6JP4HA5GQIO2V6QM7WCUGL2GZ6D4U773HMRI6RXISKPUR3

title: Registry Contract › Data types
content: AssetEntry : Field Type Notes id u64 Assigned sequentially from 1 token_contract Address The asset-token contract issuer Address Who registered it name String asset_type String real_estate \ invoice \ commodity valuation i128 USD cents created_at u32 Ledger at registration active bool Excluded from TVL when false

title: Registry Contract › initialize
content: fn initialize(env: Env, admin: Address) Sets the admin and resets the counter. Callable once. Auth: admin . Errors: AlreadyInitialized (1) .

title: Registry Contract › register_asset
content: fn register_asset( env: Env, issuer: Address, token_contract: Address, name: String, asset_type: String, valuation: i128, ) -> u64 Registers a new asset and returns its assigned id. - Auth: issuer - Errors: NotInitialized (2) , InvalidValuation (5) if valuation < 0 .

title: Registry Contract › get_asset
content: fn get_asset(env: Env, asset_id: u64) -> AssetEntry Fetches a single asset. Errors: AssetNotFound (4) .

title: Registry Contract › get_assets_by_issuer / get_assets_by_type / get_all_assets
content: fn get_assets_by_issuer(env: Env, issuer: Address) -> Vec fn get_assets_by_type(env: Env, asset_type: String) -> Vec fn get_all_assets(env: Env) -> Vec Query helpers returning filtered or complete lists. These back the API's /assets endpoint and the web app's explore page.

title: Registry Contract › deactivate_asset
content: fn deactivate_asset(env: Env, admin: Address, asset_id: u64) Marks an asset inactive; it is then excluded from TVL. Auth: admin . Errors: Unauthorized (3) , AssetNotFound (4) .

title: Registry Contract › total_value_locked / asset_count
content: fn total_value_locked(env: Env) -> i128 fn asset_count(env: Env) -> u64 total_value_locked sums valuation across active assets, in USD cents. asset_count returns the total registered (active or not).

title: Registry Contract › Code example
content: const registry = new Contract("CBX5SMLT…PUR3"); // register a freshly deployed asset token const op = registry.call( "register_asset", new Address(issuer).toScVal(), new Address(tokenContract).toScVal(), nativeToScVal("Manhattan Loft", { type: "string" }), nativeToScVal("real_estate", { type: "string" }), nativeToScVal(500_000_000n, { type: "i128" }), // $5,000,000 in cents );

title: Registry Contract › Events
content: Topic Data Emitted by ("register", issuer) id register_asset ("deactvate",) asset_id deactivate_asset

title: Registry Contract › Security considerations
content: - The registry is an index, not a source of truth for balances. Supply and balances live in the asset-token contract; the registry's valuation is the issuer-declared figure at registration (updatable on the token via update_valuation , not mirrored here automatically). - Anyone can register an asset (auth is the issuer, not the admin). Consumers should treat listing in the registry as self-attestation , and rely on the compliance contract for the actual holding restrictions. - Deactivation is admin-only and only affects TVL and listing, not the token.

title: Getting Started
description: What the Stellar RWA Toolkit is, how asset tokenization works, and how to run it.
content: Getting Started The Stellar RWA Toolkit is an end-to-end system for tokenizing real-world assets (RWAs) — real estate, invoices, commodities — on Stellar using Soroban smart contracts, with compliance enforced on-chain . It has three parts, each in its own repository: - Contracts — four Soroban contracts: asset-token , compliance , registry , dividend . - API — a Rust/Axum service that indexes all tokenized-asset activity and serves it over REST. - Web app — a Next.js front-end for issuers and investors. The toolkit is early-stage (v0.1.0) and deployed on Stellar Testnet only — there is no mainnet deployment. The contracts and API have not been externally audited . Build and experiment against Testnet, but do not use this code to custody real value until it has been independently audited and reviewed for securities compliance.

title: Getting Started › What "tokenizing a real-world asset" means
content: A real-world asset — say a $5,000,000 Manhattan loft — is represented on-chain as a fungible token. Each token is a fractional claim on the underlying asset. Unlike an ordinary token, an RWA token is compliance-gated : only addresses that have passed KYC and sit on an allowlist may hold or receive it. The gate is not a policy sitting in a database — it is enforced by the contract itself. On every transfer, the asset-token contract makes a cross-contract call into the compliance contract to check both the sender and the recipient. If either fails, the transfer reverts. Securities laws in most jurisdictions restrict who may hold a regulated asset. Enforcing that restriction in the contract — rather than in an app that can be bypassed — is what makes a token suitable to represent a regulated real-world asset. See the Compliance Guide .

title: Getting Started › How the pieces fit together
content: ┌───────────────┐ issuer / investor ──▶ │ Web app │ ──▶ Freighter ──▶ Soroban contracts └───────────────┘ │ │ events + state ┌───────────────┐ polls Soroban RPC │ analysts / bots ──▶ │ REST API │ ◀─────────────────────┘ └───────────────┘ - The web app signs and submits transactions through the user's wallet. - The API only reads: it indexes on-chain state every 10 seconds and never holds a key or signs anything.

title: Getting Started › Prerequisites
content: - Freighter browser extension (for the web app) - Node.js 18+ (web app and docs) - Rust 1.75+ (API and contracts) - The Stellar CLI (to deploy contracts)

title: Getting Started › Quickstart
content: The fastest way to see the API working is to run it locally against the deployed Testnet contracts — no wallet, no signing, no tokens required.

title: Getting Started › 1. Clone and start the API
content: git clone https://github.com/RWA-ToolKit/stellar-rwa-api-docs cd stellar-rwa-api-docs/api cp .env.example .env # Testnet contract IDs and RPC URL are pre-filled cargo run → listening on 0.0.0.0:8080 The API is ready when you see listening on 0.0.0.0:8080 in the terminal. It will start polling Soroban Testnet immediately; the first snapshot is available within ~10 seconds.

title: Getting Started › 2. Hit the live endpoints
content: Open a second terminal and run these commands against http://localhost:8080 . Data endpoints use the /v1 prefix; the liveness probe is /health . Check the liveness probe: curl http://localhost:8080/health {"status":"ok"} Fetch platform-wide stats: curl http://localhost:8080/v1/stats { "total_assets": 1, "active_assets": 1, "tvl_cents": "500000000", "tvl_usd": 5000000.0, "total_holders": 1, "total_distributions": 0, "last_indexed_ledger": 3514152, "last_updated": "2026-07-09T08:43:12.101772791+00:00" } tvl_cents is a string to avoid JavaScript precision loss; divide by 100 for dollars. last_updated is the wall-clock time of the most recent successful Soroban RPC poll. List all tokenized assets: curl http://localhost:8080/v1/assets [ { "id": 1, "contract_id": "CBMCWLSQSWUTLUJFCNBHNBSXMUM3XU7NAQ5TSNERW4HA4ZZBYHLG4ECZ", "name": "Manhattan Loft", "symbol": "MLOFT", "asset_type": "real_estate", "decimals": 7, "total_supply": "50000000000000", "valuation_cents": "500000000", "valuation_usd": 5000000.0, "active": true } ] Fetch the sample asset (id 1 ) directly: curl http://localhost:8080/v1/assets/1 { "id": 1, "contract_id": "CBMCWLSQSWUTLUJFCNBHNBSXMUM3XU7NAQ5TSNERW4HA4ZZBYHLG4ECZ", "name": "Manhattan Loft", "symbol": "MLOFT", "asset_type": "real_estate", "decimals": 7, "total_supply": "50000000000000", "valuation_cents": "500000000", "valuation_usd": 5000000.0, "active": true } The response includes an ETag and Cache-Control header. Send the returned ETag on the next request; if the indexed snapshot has not changed, the API returns 304 Not Modified with no body, so reuse your cached response: Capture the ETag from the first response curl -i http://localhost:8080/v1/assets/1 ETag: "ledger-3514152" Cache-Control: public, max-age=10 Send the ETag on a later request (use the value your response returned) curl -i -H 'If-None-Match: "ledger-3514152"' http://localhost:8080/v1/assets/1 HTTP/1.1 304 Not Modified Check token holders for asset 1 : curl http://localhost:8080/v1/assets/1/holders [ { "address": "GAIQGTOBTTLLDJ4SWGGESM7UWJ2DI4K3ZNHUSHPDKJL2IE5FKY3BSRAA", "balance": "50000000000000", "share_percent": 100.0 } ] Both the asset list and holder list support offset and limit query parameters. offset is the number of records to skip (starting at 0); limit defaults to 50 and is capped at 100: First and second pages of assets (20 per page) curl 'http://localhost:8080/v1/assets?offset=0&limit=20' curl 'http://localhost:8080/v1/assets?offset=20&limit=20' First 10 holders, then the next 10 for asset 1 curl 'http://localhost:8080/v1/assets/1/holders?offset=0&limit=10' curl 'http://localhost:8080/v1/assets/1/holders?offset=10&limit=10' Check the compliance summary for asset 1 : curl http://localhost:8080/v1/assets/1/compliance { "asset_id": 1, "total_approved": 1, "total_suspended": 0, "total_expired": 0 } Your last_indexed_ledger and last_updated values will differ from the examples above — they reflect the ledger height at the time your local indexer ran. Everything else should match the sample Testnet deployment.

title: Getting Started › 3. Run the docs site
content: cd ../docs npm install npm run dev # http://localhost:3000

title: Getting Started › Environment variables
content: The API reads the following environment variables: Variable Default Description RWA_RPC_URL https://soroban-testnet.stellar.org Soroban RPC endpoint the indexer polls RWA_CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS http://localhost:3000 Comma-separated browser origin allowlist RWA_RATE_LIMIT_PER_SECOND 5 Sustained requests allowed per client IP each second RWA_RATE_LIMIT_BURST 20 Maximum per-client request burst RWA_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_SECS 30 Maximum request duration in seconds RWA_MAX_BODY_BYTES 1048576 Maximum request body size in bytes RWA_REGISTRY_ID CBX5SMLTXX6JP4HA5GQIO2V6QM7WCUGL2GZ6D4U773HMRI6RXISKPUR3 Deployed registry contract id (Testnet) RWA_DIVIDEND_ID CAR4XY3CEBQWFOL27JEWFW34KXSIZA7RFKDQMEIV7ZU723RWY37I2SYX Deployed dividend contract id (Testnet) RWA_READ_SOURCE GAIQGTOBTTLLDJ4SWGGESM7UWJ2DI4K3ZNHUSHPDKJL2IE5FKY3BSRAA Funded account used as source for read simulations (must exist on the RPC) RWA_METRICS_TOKEN (none) Bearer token required by /metrics ; requests are denied when unset PORT 8080 HTTP server port RUST_LOG stellar_rwa_api=info,tower_http=warn Log filter (tracing-subscriber format) The .env.example file includes Testnet defaults. Copy it and adjust as needed for your network.

title: Getting Started › Running with Docker
content: Build and run the API in a container: cd stellar-rwa-api-docs/api docker build -t stellar-rwa-api . docker run -p 8080:8080 \ -e RWA_RPC_URL=https://soroban-testnet.stellar.org \ -e RWA_REGISTRY_ID=CBX5SMLTXX6JP4HA5GQIO2V6QM7WCUGL2GZ6D4U773HMRI6RXISKPUR3 \ -e RWA_DIVIDEND_ID=CAR4XY3CEBQWFOL27JEWFW34KXSIZA7RFKDQMEIV7ZU723RWY37I2SYX \ -e RWA_READ_SOURCE=GAIQGTOBTTLLDJ4SWGGESM7UWJ2DI4K3ZNHUSHPDKJL2IE5FKY3BSRAA \ -e PORT=8080 \ stellar-rwa-api Or use an .env file: docker run -p 8080:8080 --env-file .env stellar-rwa-api Then run the same curl commands from step 2 against http://localhost:8080 .

title: Getting Started › Network guide
content: Everything is deployed on Testnet . The network passphrase is: Test SDF Network ; September 2015 Point Freighter at Testnet and fund your account with the friendbot before interacting. These contracts are deployed on Testnet for demonstration. Do not use them to custody real value. A mainnet deployment requires a full securities-compliance and legal review.

title: Getting Started › Mainnet integration
content: The Testnet settings above are not interchangeable with Mainnet. Before pointing an integration at Mainnet, set and verify each network-specific value: Setting Testnet Mainnet Network passphrase Test SDF Network ; September 2015 Public Global Stellar Network ; September 2015 Soroban RPC https://soroban-testnet.stellar.org Use a Mainnet Soroban RPC URL from your chosen provider; endpoint URLs and access terms are provider-specific. Contract IDs The Testnet IDs listed below Deploy the contracts to Mainnet and use the resulting Mainnet IDs. Contract IDs are network-specific; this project does not publish a Mainnet deployment. Read source An account that exists on Testnet Set RWA_READ_SOURCE to a valid account on Mainnet that your RPC can use for simulation. Fees Testnet XLM has no real-world value Mainnet transactions and deployments consume real XLM. Base and Soroban resource fees vary; simulate and assemble transactions to estimate fees rather than copying a Testnet fee. For the API, set RWA_RPC_URL , RWA_REGISTRY_ID , and RWA_DIVIDEND_ID to Mainnet values. The service requires explicit registry and dividend IDs whenever the RPC URL is not the default Testnet endpoint. Configure the asset-token and compliance IDs in any client that calls those contracts directly. The API's read-only simulations do not submit transactions; deployments and writes do incur Mainnet fees. See the Integration Guide for the simulate-and-assemble flow.

Continue to the Compliance Guide — the concept that makes this an RWA platform rather than a plain token factory.

title: Integration Guide
description: Query the API, use the TypeScript examples, and call the contracts directly.
content: Integration Guide Examples in this guide use Testnet endpoints, contract IDs, and passphrase. For the corresponding Mainnet configuration—including provider RPC URL, new contract IDs, and real XLM fee considerations—see Mainnet integration . Three ways to integrate with the platform, from easiest to most direct: 1. Query the REST API — indexed, JSON, no XDR. 2. Read contracts via the JS SDK — live simulation of view calls. 3. Submit transactions — sign with Freighter and invoke contract methods.

title: Integration Guide › End-to-end read workflow
content: The REST API is the simplest integration surface. It is read-only and returns plain JSON. Follow this path to discover an asset, read its details, check an address against the asset's live compliance gate, and list its distributions. Set API_BASE_URL to the API origin (for example, http://localhost:8080 ); the versioned data routes use the /v1 prefix. 1. Discover assets and choose a registry id from the response. curl "$API_BASE_URL/v1/assets" 2. Read the chosen asset. Note its compliance_contract and id. curl "$API_BASE_URL/v1/assets/1" 3. Check an address against that asset's live on-chain compliance gate. Use the compliance_contract from the asset response and a valid simulation source account; no signing or submission is needed: Account, Address, BASE_FEE, Contract, Networks, TransactionBuilder, rpc, scValToNative, } from "@stellar/stellar-sdk"; const server = new rpc.Server("https://soroban-testnet.stellar.org"); const complianceContract = " "; const investor = " "; const source = new Account( "GAIQGTOBTTLLDJ4SWGGESM7UWJ2DI4K3ZNHUSHPDKJL2IE5FKY3BSRAA", "0", ); const tx = new TransactionBuilder(source, { fee: BASE_FEE, networkPassphrase: Networks.TESTNET, }) .addOperation(new Contract(complianceContract).call( "is_allowed", new Address(investor).toScVal(), )) .setTimeout(30) .build(); const sim = await server.simulateTransaction(tx); if (rpc.Api.isSimulationError(sim)) throw new Error(sim.error); const allowed = scValToNative(sim.result!.retval) as boolean; console.log({ investor, allowed }); 4. List distributions for the same registry id. curl "$API_BASE_URL/v1/assets/1/dividends" The /v1/compliance/:address API route is an indexed view of an address's current holdings, not a live compliance-contract check. Use is_allowed above when deciding whether a transfer will pass the on-chain gate. The indexer refreshes about every 10 seconds, so API data may lag current contract state.

title: Integration Guide › TypeScript client
content: const API = ${process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL ?? "http://localhost:8080"}/v1 ; id: number; token_contract: string; name: string; symbol: string; asset_type: string; valuation_cents: string; valuation_usd: number; decimals: number; total_supply: string; holders: number; active: boolean; paused: boolean; compliance_contract: string; } const res = await fetch( ${API}/assets , { cache: "no-store" }); if (!res.ok) throw new Error( API ${res.status} ); return res.json(); } // Amounts are strings (i128) — parse with BigInt and format by decimals. const raw = BigInt(a.total_supply); const base = 10n ** BigInt(a.decimals); return (Number(raw) / Number(base)).toLocaleString(); } Always parse valuation_cents , total_supply , balance , and total_amount with BigInt(...) — they are decimal strings to preserve i128 precision.

title: Integration Guide › Reading contracts directly
content: To read live state without the API, simulate a view call with the Stellar JS SDK. No signing is required for reads. Contract, TransactionBuilder, Account, BASE_FEE, Networks, rpc, scValToNative, } from "@stellar/stellar-sdk"; const server = new rpc.Server("https://soroban-testnet.stellar.org"); const REGISTRY = "CBX5SMLTXX6JP4HA5GQIO2V6QM7WCUGL2GZ6D4U773HMRI6RXISKPUR3"; const contract = new Contract(REGISTRY); // Any valid account works as the simulation source. const source = new Account( "GAIQGTOBTTLLDJ4SWGGESM7UWJ2DI4K3ZNHUSHPDKJL2IE5FKY3BSRAA", "0", ); const tx = new TransactionBuilder(source, { fee: BASE_FEE, networkPassphrase: Networks.TESTNET, }) .addOperation(contract.call("total_value_locked")) .setTimeout(30) .build(); const sim = await server.simulateTransaction(tx); if (rpc.Api.isSimulationError(sim)) throw new Error(sim.error); return scValToNative(sim.result!.retval) as bigint; // USD cents } Check an address's compliance status the same way: const COMPLIANCE = "CBUERYDM7DXTZLLKDBRJKUBPFJ7M4OSUN4T7XKUARU345RLXNAIQD2IU"; const op = new Contract(COMPLIANCE).call( "is_allowed", new Address(investor).toScVal(), ); // build → simulate → scValToNative(retval) === boolean

title: Integration Guide › Submitting transactions
content: Writes must be signed by the account that authorizes them. In the browser, sign with Freighter: Contract, TransactionBuilder, Networks, BASE_FEE, rpc, Address, nativeToScVal, } from "@stellar/stellar-sdk"; const server = new rpc.Server("https://soroban-testnet.stellar.org"); token: string, from: string, to: string, amount: bigint, ): Promise { const account = await server.getAccount(from); const op = new Contract(token).call( "transfer", new Address(from).toScVal(), new Address(to).toScVal(), nativeToScVal(amount, { type: "i128" }), ); const built = new TransactionBuilder(account, { fee: BASE_FEE, networkPassphrase: Networks.TESTNET, }).addOperation(op).setTimeout(60).build(); // Simulate + assemble to attach the Soroban footprint and resource fees. const sim = await server.simulateTransaction(built); if (rpc.Api.isSimulationError(sim)) throw new Error(sim.error); const prepared = rpc.assembleTransaction(built, sim).build(); const { signedTxXdr } = await signTransaction(prepared.toXDR(), { networkPassphrase: Networks.TESTNET, address: from, }); const signed = TransactionBuilder.fromXDR(signedTxXdr, Networks.TESTNET); const sent = await server.sendTransaction(signed); return sent.hash; // then poll server.getTransaction(hash) } A transfer will revert with SenderNotCompliant (7) or RecipientNotCompliant (8) if either party is not KYC-approved. Check is_allowed for both addresses before submitting to give users a clear error up front.

title: Integration Guide › Retries, failover and rate limits
content: Public Soroban RPC endpoints are shared infrastructure: expect occasional network errors, 503 s and 429 s. The reference API's indexer ( api/src/indexer/mod.rs ) handles this as described below; a client that calls RPC directly (as in the sections above) should follow the same pattern.

title: Integration Guide › Retry guidance
content: What the reference indexer does for each simulateTransaction read: Setting Value Attempts per read (first try + retries) 4 ( MAX_READ_ATTEMPTS ) Base delay 150 ms, doubling per attempt Maximum delay 2 s Jitter Full jitter: a random delay in [0, cap] - Retried in place: only transport errors (connection failures, dropped or unreadable responses) and JSON-RPC or simulation errors returned in a 2xx response. - Not retried: XDR, strkey and JSON decode errors. These come from how the request was built or the response was parsed, so they fail the same way on every attempt. Other non- 2xx HTTP statuses (for example 502 ) are not retried in place either; the read fails and the refresh is retried on the next cycle. - Failed refresh: if a read still fails, the whole refresh is abandoned, the API keeps serving the last good snapshot, and the indexer tries again after the 10 s poll interval. For your own client: retry only idempotent calls ( simulateTransaction , getLedgerEntries , getTransaction ), use capped exponential backoff with full jitter so clients don't retry in lockstep, and keep the retry budget well under your polling interval. Do not blindly re-send a sendTransaction after a timeout. Poll getTransaction with the hash first, because the transaction may already have been accepted.

title: Integration Guide › Failover
content: The reference API does not fail over between RPC endpoints. It reads a single RWA_RPC_URL (default https://soroban-testnet.stellar.org ). If that endpoint is down, the indexer keeps serving the last good snapshot and last_indexed_ledger in GET /v1/stats stops advancing. Watch that value, or the rwa_indexer_refresh_total{outcome="failure"} metric, to detect an outage. To switch providers, change RWA_RPC_URL and restart. A non-testnet URL also requires RWA_REGISTRY_ID and RWA_DIVIDEND_ID . If your own client needs failover, keep an ordered list of RPC URLs for the same network . Move to the next URL only after its retry budget runs out, not on the first error. Compare latestLedger across providers so you don't read from a node that is lagging behind.

title: Integration Guide › Rate-limit interaction
content: - A 429 Too Many Requests or 503 Service Unavailable from RPC is not retried in place. Fast retries would only add load to a node that is already pushing back. The read fails, the refresh cycle ends, and the next cycle waits for the Retry-After header (integer seconds). If that header is missing or not an integer, it waits the normal 10 s poll interval instead. - Retries count against the provider's rate limit. With 4 attempts per read, a single refresh can make up to 4× the normal number of requests during an incident. Size your request rate with that in mind. - The REST API applies its own per-IP token-bucket limit to your client ( RWA_RATE_LIMIT_PER_SECOND / RWA_RATE_LIMIT_BURST ). Handle its 429 the same way and honour Retry-After . See Rate Limits & Caching .

title: Integration Guide › Contract addresses
content: All Testnet contract ids are listed in Getting Started . Asset-token contract ids are discovered from the registry's get_all_assets (or the API's /assets ).

title: Indexer Metrics
description: Prometheus metrics exposed by the Stellar RWA API indexer.
content: Indexer Metrics GET /metrics (bearer token via RWA_METRICS_TOKEN ) exposes Prometheus text format. Names follow Prometheus conventions: rwa_indexer_ prefix, base units in the suffix ( _seconds ), and _total for counters. Metric Type Description rwa_indexer_refresh_duration_seconds histogram Poll (refresh cycle) duration. rwa_indexer_refresh_total{outcome} counter Refresh cycles, outcome is success or failure . Failures are the failure series. rwa_indexer_asset_read_errors_total{asset_id,read} counter Failed per-asset RPC reads. rwa_indexer_last_indexed_ledger gauge Ledger of the latest successful snapshot. rwa_indexer_last_success_timestamp_seconds gauge Unix time of the last successful refresh. rwa_indexer_last_success_age_seconds gauge Lag: seconds since the last successful refresh, computed at scrape time. rwa_indexer_snapshot_assets gauge Assets in the in-memory snapshot. rwa_indexer_snapshot_events gauge Events in the in-memory snapshot. Suggested alert: rwa_indexer_last_success_age_seconds > 60 .

title: Snapshot Memory
content: Snapshot Memory The indexer keeps a full snapshot (assets, holders, compliance, dividends, stats) in memory and rebuilds it every poll. Request handlers currently take a full Snapshot::clone() per request.

title: Snapshot Memory › Measurement
content: Each refresh records: - rwa_indexer_snapshot_estimated_bytes - approximate payload size (JSON length of every collection). Plot it against rwa_indexer_snapshot_assets to get bytes per asset; growth is linear in assets and in holders per asset. - rwa_indexer_snapshot_clone_duration_seconds - time of one full clone, which is the extra per-request cost of the current design.

title: Snapshot Memory › Strategy
content: 1. Serve requests from a shared Arc (the ArcSwap guard already provides one), so a request costs a pointer copy instead of a deep clone. 2. Cap per-asset holder lists in the snapshot and page the remainder on demand once rwa_indexer_snapshot_estimated_bytes approaches the container limit. 3. Alert on rwa_indexer_snapshot_estimated_bytes growth per asset before changing storage (a database is the step after paging).

title: Time & Ledgers
description: Understanding the ledger-sequence time model used across contracts and the API.
content: Time & Ledgers Throughout the Stellar RWA contracts and API, time is never expressed as a wall-clock timestamp. Instead, all time values use Stellar ledger sequence numbers — a monotonically increasing counter that increments roughly every 5 seconds on the Stellar network. This design eliminates time-sync issues and makes on-chain logic deterministic.

title: Time & Ledgers › Why ledger sequences?
content: - No clock skew. A ledger number is determined by network consensus, not server clocks. - Deterministic ordering. You can always compare ledger numbers to know which event happened first, without worrying about timestamp precision. - Simpler contracts. No need to worry about wall-clock adjustments or leap seconds.

title: Time & Ledgers › Ledger sequences in contracts
content: All on-chain time fields are u32 ledger sequence numbers: - Compliance contract: verified_at , expires_at (approval expiry) - Dividend contract: created_at (when a distribution was announced) - Registry contract: created_at (when an asset was registered) - Asset-token contract: clawback_at (when a clawback was performed)

title: Time & Ledgers › The special case: expires_at = 0 means "never"
content: When an expiry field (like expires_at in the compliance allowlist) is set to 0 , it means the permission never expires . This is a universal convention across all contracts: // Add a user to the allowlist with no expiry const op = compliance.call( "add_to_allowlist", admin, userAddress, "US", 0 // expires_at = 0 means never expires ); To set an expiry, provide a future ledger number: const server = new Horizon.Server("https://horizon.stellar.org"); const ledgers = await server.ledgers().limit(1).order("desc").call(); const now = ledgers.records[0].sequence; // Approve for 1 year (~6.3 million ledgers at ~5s per ledger) const expiresAt = now + 6_300_000; const op = compliance.call( "add_to_allowlist", admin, userAddress, "US", expiresAt );

title: Time & Ledgers › Checking expiry at runtime
content: The compliance contract's is_allowed gate checks expiry like this: // User is approved if: // (expires_at == 0) -- never expires, OR // (now = expires_at , the approval is considered expired and is_allowed returns false , blocking all transfers. No on-chain cron job is needed — expiry is enforced at read time.

title: Time & Ledgers › Ledger sequences in the API
content: The REST API mirrors this design. All time fields in responses are ledger sequence numbers , never wall-clock timestamps:

title: Time & Ledgers › Assets endpoint
content: { "id": 1, "name": "Manhattan Loft", "created_at_ledger": 3502885, "total_supply": "1000000" }

title: Time & Ledgers › Compliance endpoint
content: { "address": "GBUQWP...", "status": "Approved", "jurisdiction": "US", "verified_at": 3500000, "expires_at": 9800000, "expired": false } The expired field is a convenience boolean: true if expires_at != 0 && expires_at <= last_indexed_ledger .

title: Time & Ledgers › Dividends endpoint
content: { "id": 1, "asset_id": 1, "per_share_cents": "100", "created_at_ledger": 3510000, "payable_at_ledger": 3520000, "claimed": 500 }

title: Time & Ledgers › Converting ledger numbers to wall-clock time
description: Converting ledger numbers to wall-clock time
content: To convert a ledger number to an approximate wall-clock time, use the Horizon API: const server = new Horizon.Server("https://horizon.stellar.org"); const ledger = await server.ledgers().ledger(3502885).call(); console.log(ledger.closed_at); // "2026-05-15T10:30:00Z" Each ledger also records the wall-clock time it was closed, which you can use to estimate when a given ledger sequence number occurred. Rule of thumb: Stellar produces ~1 ledger per 5 seconds, so a ledger 1 million in the future is roughly 58 days away.

title: Time & Ledgers › Handling expires_at in your integration
content: When building an integration against the API: 1. Display the ledger number and the expired boolean. Don't try to calculate expiry yourself; trust the expired field from the API. 2. Refresh approval before expiry. If you're tracking approval expiry, call add_to_allowlist again before the expires_at ledger is reached. 3. Remember expires_at = 0 means never. Don't treat 0 as an epoch or default timestamp. 4. Use the API's expired field. The API already handles the comparison against the current indexed ledger for you.

title: Time & Ledgers › Common mistakes
content: - Treating ledger numbers as timestamps: They are not microseconds, milliseconds, or any other time unit. They are ledger sequence numbers only. - Forgetting that 0 means "never": Setting expires_at: 0 will create an approval that never expires, which may not be what you intended. - Assuming expiry is checked by a cron job: Expiry is enforced at read time ( is_allowed ). Once the current ledger passes expires_at , the approval is immediately and deterministically considered expired. - Comparing ledger numbers across different chains: Each Stellar network (testnet, public, futurenet) has its own ledger sequence counter. Do not assume a ledger sequence is portable between networks.

title: Web App Guide
description: Connect Freighter, tokenize an asset, manage compliance, and distribute dividends.
content: Web App Guide The web app is the front-end for issuers and investors. It signs and submits every transaction through the user's Freighter wallet — it never holds keys. This guide walks through the main flows.

title: Web App Guide › Connecting Freighter
content: 1. Install the Freighter browser extension and create or import an account. 2. Switch Freighter to Testnet and fund the account via the friendbot . 3. In the app, click Connect Wallet and approve the connection. The app follows Freighter's selected network while connected, so reads and writes always target the same network. Your address appears in the header with a menu to copy it, view it on Stellar Expert, or disconnect. While disconnected you can still browse assets read-only and switch networks with the network selector. Once connected, the app locks to your wallet's network.

title: Web App Guide › Tokenizing an asset (issuer)
content: Open Tokenize an Asset and complete the multi-step form: 1. Asset info — name, type (real estate / invoice / commodity), description, and USD valuation. 2. Token config — symbol, total supply, and decimals. 3. Compliance — the initial set of KYC-approved addresses and their jurisdictions. Your own issuer address must be included , because the token mints the initial supply to you and that mint is compliance-gated. 4. Review & deploy — the app deploys the compliance contract and asset-token contract, then registers the asset in the registry. On success you get the deployed contract addresses with Stellar Expert links. Deployment is several transactions — a compliance contract, a token contract, and a registry registration. Approve each in Freighter as prompted. If you approve yourself last, the initial mint will fail; approve the issuer address in the compliance step first.

title: Web App Guide › Managing the compliance allowlist (issuer)
content: From the Issuer → Compliance page, select one of your assets: - Add an address — enter the account, choose a jurisdiction, and set an optional expiry. This calls add_to_allowlist and sets the status to Approved . - Suspend / remove — temporarily hold or permanently delete an approval. - Block a jurisdiction — freeze every holder in a country at once. The allowlist table shows each record's status, jurisdiction, and expiry. See the Compliance Guide for the model behind these actions.

title: Web App Guide › Creating dividend distributions (issuer)
content: From Issuer → Dividends , select an asset and open Create Distribution : 1. Choose the payment token (e.g. USDC on Stellar). 2. Enter the total amount to distribute. 3. Submit — the app calls create_distribution , which escrows the funds in the dividend contract. Holders then claim their proportional share. Each distribution shows a progress bar of claimed vs. total.

title: Web App Guide › Investor: compliance status and holdings
content: As an investor you can: - Check your compliance status on any asset's detail page and in your Portfolio . The app reads is_allowed and your KycRecord , and shows Approved / Pending / Suspended / Rejected / Not Registered . - Hold and transfer an asset — but only if you are approved. The transfer form is disabled with an explanatory message whenever you are not KYC-approved, the asset is paused, or your balance is zero. - Claim dividends — the app shows your claimable amount per distribution and a one-click Claim button that calls claim . If your transfer is blocked, the app tells you why — pending approval, suspension, a blocked jurisdiction, an expired approval, or simply not being on the allowlist. Ask the asset's issuer to approve your address. This is the compliance gate, not a bug.

title: Web App Guide › Data paths: API-backed vs. direct-RPC
content: The web app supports two distinct data paths for reading platform state, asset details, and aggregates (such as TVL, holder counts, and distribution progress): 1. API-backed path : When configured with NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL , the web app fetches pre-computed aggregates and lists from the REST API ( /stats , /assets , /holders , /dividends , etc.). 2. Direct-RPC simulation fallback : When the API base URL is not configured, the web app falls back to simulating contract view calls directly against Soroban RPC using the Stellar JS SDK.

title: Web App Guide › Freshness and cost tradeoffs
content: Dimension API-Backed Path Direct-RPC Fallback Path Freshness Eventual consistency (~10s lag behind ledger tip, governed by indexer polling interval). Real-time state directly from the current ledger head. Client Performance Fast; single HTTP GET request returning lightweight JSON. No client-side XDR decoding. Slower; requires executing transaction simulations and decoding ScVal responses ( scValToNative ). RPC Load & Cost Low; only the background indexer polls Soroban RPC every 10 seconds. Scales efficiently for many concurrent users. High; every client browser directly simulates contract calls, generating heavy RPC volume and risk of rate limiting. Trust Model Relies on the API service cache as an intermediary. Trustless; queries the Stellar network directly without intermediaries.

title: Web App Guide › When to choose each
content: - Choose the API-backed path for production web app deployments, public dashboards, and high-traffic environments where fast load times, scalability, and conservation of Soroban RPC limits are paramount. - Choose the direct-RPC path for local development without running the indexer API, trustless setups where users must query the blockchain directly without trusting an intermediate cache, or when strict real-time precision at ledger head is required. See the Architecture Overview for how the indexer works and the Integration Guide for code examples of both querying the REST API and reading contracts directly via the JS SDK.

title: Web App Guide › Transaction feedback
content: Every on-chain action shows live progress — preparing → awaiting signature → submitting → confirming — and, on success, a link to the transaction on Stellar Expert. Contract errors are translated into plain-language messages.
